_comment: The docs graph's SUB-GRAPHS, declared from within (issue #1164; the owner's #980 ruling that nesting is sanctioned when a node inside the outer directory labels what it holds). Same shape as `beans/beans.json` and an instance's `<instance>.json` — `ContentDirectorySchema` entries, paths relative to THIS file's directory. Each kind here declares `within: "docs"` in the registry, which is what folds it under Docs in every list of kinds.
name: cat-harness

directories.description: Proposals for this harness's own features — initial analysis, MVP, options — argued, and updated in place, before and while they are built.

What this harness promises, one page per shipped feature: a proposal MOVED here when its feature ships, its front matter a `Requirement` (`bootstrap/schemas/requirement.schema.json`), checked by `check:requirements`.
Start here: installing, getting started, contributing and accessibility.
Concepts: what the harness, the knowledge graph and their parts are.
Authoring guides: how to do a task with the harness, one guide per task.
Process & methodology: the publication workflow, CRDM and what counts as evidence.
FHIR: FHIR content and the IG Publisher.

Derived indexes over the other graphs — one page per auto-doc TYPE crossed with each SUB-GRAPH that type reaches, written by `scripts/gen-auto-docs.ts` and never by hand. Its own sub-sub-graphs are named from within by `auto-docs.json`, which is GENERATED from that script's `TYPES` so there is one answer to what types exist. The path is `cat-harness/auto-docs` rather than `auto-docs` because `viewerPlacement` puts a handler's output at `<base>/<handler>/<kind>/`, and the handler segment is part of the route rather than an accident (bean `06e3`, owner 2026-09-21: THE HANDLER WINS).

The UML overview PAGES — one per instance and one per declared sub-graph, written by `scripts/gen-uml-overview.ts` (its `DOCS_ROOT`, line 74) and never by hand. 134 files on `main` at the time of declaring. `auto-docs` rather than a kind of its own, on the same argument as `beans.json`'s `defs` and `archive` both declaring `bean-defs`: a sub-graph's identity is its directory id, and a kind per writer would be a registry entry restating one sentence. **The path is `uml/overview`, never `uml`, and that is load-bearing**: `cat-harness/uml/` holds this generator's 266 `.puml`/`.mmd` files PLUS `harness-object-model.puml`, `harness-schemas.puml` and a README from other writers, and `docs/assets/img/uml/` holds four SVGs from `gen-object-model-uml.ts` beside the 266 under `overview/`. One writer per directory holds at the `overview` level and fails one level up. Bean `xsrv`; no `storage` is set here — see the sibling entry. The id is `uml-overview-pages` rather than the obvious `uml-overview` because that name is already a skill (`skills/kg/kg-core/uml-overview`) and a Tool node; a directory id and a skill id may well be separate namespaces, but a declaration is not the place to find out.

The rendered SVGs for the pages above — same generator, its `SVG_ROOT` (line 76), 266 files on `main`. Beside each SVG, the same model as Graphviz DOT (`<name>.dot`), which the page's Interactive view fetches and lays out in the browser (`assets/js/kg-graph.js`, skill `kg-subgraph-layout`): published here because the reader's browser fetches it, where the `.puml` and `.mmd` under `uml/overview/` are only linked. A separate entry rather than one covering both because they are two directories with two paths, and a declaration states where to look. **`storage` is deliberately NOT set on either entry.** `DirectoryStorageSchema`'s docblock, §"Not yet set on any declaration": *"Setting it earlier would tell the presence checks to stop looking while the readers still read the checkout."* So the order is declare, seed the branch, migrate `uml:overview:check`, and only then flip — `xsrv`'s Done-when 1 bundles the first and last of those into one line, and this is the first.

The docs graph's own SOURCE: one directory per generated page (`<group>-<slug>/`), holding its authored blocks (`.md`), its content-object manifests (`.ts`, `prose` and `webpage`) and their generated `.jsonld`. `gen-docs-pages.ts` renders each into the page beside it (`docs/<group>/<slug>.md`); Jekyll excludes this directory (`_config.yml`), so a block is never published as a page of its own. Moved here from `content/docs/` on 2026-10-09 (owner: "move content/docs into docs/"), so the docs subgraph carries its own source and a mount of `docs` brings it.
